notes.text: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to gain control of the brakes of a trailer, modify the firmware, disable the brake lights, modify the brake conditions or disable other critical safety features.
notes.title: Advisory Summary

notes.text: This product is provided subject to this Notification (https://www.cisa.gov/notification) and this Privacy & Use policy (https://www.cisa.gov/privacy-policy).
notes.title: Legal Notice and Terms of Use

notes.text: CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks: Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages. Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams. Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time.

notes.title: Vulnerability Summary

remediations.details: Elecbrakes has released updated firmware (EB2 3.0.4.4.3). Users should open the Elecbrakes app and install the firmware update.

This device is the predecessor to the EB2 and the VM1 and is no longer sold. The vendor is determining how to address these vulnerabilities for this particular controller.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC2000

notes.text: No replay or command-integrity protection. Commands lack sequence numbers, nonces, or session tokens; captured commands can be replayed, and the last command persists across sessions.

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Access Control in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC2000

notes.text: The affected product has an unauthenticated command injection, which may allow an in-range BLE device to gain access to write to the control interface and influence braking with no authentication or pairing.
notes.title: Vulnerability Summary

notes.text: Elecbrakes reports no known incidents of damage or injury from this vulnerability. Elecbrakes is actively working to determine a remediation plan. Users are encouraged to periodically check the Elecbrakes app for any updates to the ELBC2000. If users have any questions or need any assistance, they should reach out to Elecbrakes directly.
notes.title: Vendor statement from Elecbrakes

notes.text: Elecbrakes reports no known incidents of damage or injury from this vulnerability.
